name: Carrefour France
notes: Largest single customer at 6.0% of group revenue. Contract CTR-FR-CAR-2026 carries a EUR 0.85 per undelivered unit penalty and a 3% quarterly turnover rebate if fill rate falls below 97%. Annual range review is scheduled for November 2026, which makes a sustained out-of-stock a delisting risk on top of the penalty exposure.

name: E.Leclerc
notes: Second-largest French account and the strongest performer on the Gourmet range. Penalty of EUR 0.72 per undelivered unit. Historically flexible on short-term substitution if notified early; accepted a plain-yogurt swap during the 2024 shortage.

name: Intermarché
notes: Growth account with a rising Kids pouch listing. No contractual penalty clause, which makes it the lowest-cost place to absorb an allocation cut, but the commercial team is protecting a 2027 range expansion negotiation.

name: REWE Group Deutschland
notes: Anchor German account. Contract CTR-DE-REW-2026 sets a EUR 1.05 per undelivered unit penalty, the harshest branded clause in the portfolio, plus a 4% quarterly rebate below a 97% fill rate. Also includes a supplier-emissions improvement clause requiring year-on-year Scope 3 intensity reduction.

name: EDEKA Zentrale
notes: Second German anchor with a strong organic listing on SKU-YOG-009. Penalty of EUR 0.68 per undelivered unit. Regional buying structure means allocation must be communicated through seven regional desks, which slows the notification cycle by roughly 24 hours.

name: Kaufland Deutschland
notes: Newer German account added in 2020. No penalty clause. Price-led buying behaviour and a low switching cost, so an extended out-of-stock carries real substitution risk to a competitor brand.

name: Delhaize Belgium
notes: Primary Belgian account and the largest buyer of the Gourmet dessert range. Penalty of EUR 0.95 per undelivered unit. Requires a Halal claim on the Kids dessert listing, which removes gelatin as a reformulation option for SKU-DES-004.

name: Carrefour Belgium
notes: Belgian arm buys independently of Carrefour France but coordination is expected on any allocation decision to avoid inconsistent messaging between the two entities.

name: Sodexo France
notes: Institutional catering into schools and hospitals with the highest SLA in the portfolio at 98%. Penalty of EUR 1.20 per undelivered unit, the highest per-unit exposure in the book. Contract requires 30 days notice of any specification change, which effectively rules out an emergency reformulation on their volume.

name: Compass Group Deutschland
notes: Smaller German foodservice account with a tolerant substitution clause. Willing to accept SKU-YOG-012 plain skyr in place of the fruited Pro SKU, which makes it a natural first absorber of an allocation cut.

name: Colruyt Group
notes: Private-label manufacturing contract with the harshest terms in the book: EUR 1.15 per undelivered unit plus a right of termination if fill rate falls below 95% in two consecutive quarters. No brand-equity upside to offset the exposure, so the allocation model must weight this account on pure penalty economics.

name: Metro Cash & Carry
notes: Cash and carry wholesale with order-to-order pricing and no firm commitment. Lowest allocation priority under the standard-tier 0.85 multiplier and the least costly volume to cut.
